title: Numeric and Geometric Patterns: Sequences, Rules and the nth Term
seo_title: Grade 7 Numeric and Geometric Patterns Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Investigate and extend numeric and geometric patterns looking for relationships between numbers, including patterns represented in physical or diagram form, not limited to sequences involving a constant difference or ratio, of learners' own creation, and represented in tables; describe and justify the general rules for observed relationships between numbers in own words.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 7 patterns worksheets: number sequences, constant difference and ratio, the rule for the nth term and pattern tables. 100 questions with memos.
key_sub: Check the rule on every term.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A pattern with a constant difference: 5, 9, 13, 17 … (+ 4).
  • A pattern with a constant ratio: 3, 6, 12, 24 … (× 2).
  • The rule links the term to the term number n: 4n + 1 gives 5, 9, 13 …
  • To check if a number is in the pattern, solve the rule for n: it must be a whole number.

Examples

Example

7, 12, 17, 22, …

difference 5

5n + 2

Answer: term 50 = 252

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
One difference onlyCheck all the differences.
Term or term number?n is the position.
Forgetting the constant5n + 2, not 5n.

A rule for any term using its position n.

items.q: Find the nth term of the sequence −10, −15, −20, −25, …
items.e: The difference is −5, so the sequence is like −5n. The zero term is −10 + 5 = −5. So the nth term is −5n − 5.

items.q: Find the nth term of the sequence 15, 21, 27, 33, …

items.q: The nth term of a sequence is 8n + 4. Which of these numbers is in the sequence?
items.e: 8n + 4 = 164 gives n = (164 − 4) ÷ 8 = 20, a whole number. The others do not give whole numbers. So 164.

items.q: The pattern continues. How many tiles will Figure 5 have?
items.e: Count: 1, 3, 5. Each figure adds 2 tiles: Figure 4 has 7 and Figure 5 has 9. 7 is Figure 4. 10 is 5 × 2 and forgets that Figure 1 has only 1 tile.

items.q: What term value is missing from the table?
items.e: The values go up by 5: 11 + 5 = 16. Check: 16 + 5 = 21. 3 is the term number, not the term value. 31 is the next term after 26.

items.q: The pattern continues. What is the value of term 6?
items.e: Add 6 each time: term 5 is 28 and term 6 is 34. 28 is term 5. 40 makes 6 jumps from term 1, but from term 1 to term 6 there are only 5 jumps.

items.q: The pattern continues in the same way. What is the missing term value?
items.e: The values go up by 4 each term. The term number jumps from 3 to 6, which is 3 terms: 13 + 3 × 4 = 25. 17 adds 4 only once. 21 is term 5 and 29 is term 7.

items.q: Figure 2 is hidden. The pattern grows at a constant rate. How many cubes are in Figure 2?
items.e: Figure 1 has 6 cubes and Figure 3 has 12. From Figure 1 to Figure 3 is 2 equal steps of 3: 6, 9, 12. 18 adds Figures 1 and 3.

items.q: One term value in this table is wrong. Which one?
items.e: The pattern goes up by 6: 7, 13, 19, 25, 31. 26 should be 25.

items.q: The pattern continues. What is the value of term 7?
items.e: Subtract 4 each time: 38, 34, 30, 26. 30 is term 6 and 22 is term 8. 43 subtracts 7, the term number.

items.q: Which list gives the term values of 3n + 4 for term numbers 1, 2, 3 and 4?
What is the missing value for term number 0?
items.e: The values go up by 5, so go back one step from term 1: 9 − 5 = 4. This is the initial value. 0 thinks term 0 must have value 0. 5 is the constant rate.

items.q: The pattern continues. Which figure has 40 chairs?
items.e: The rule is 2n + 2 (4, 6, 8 chairs). Solve 2n + 2 = 40: 40 − 2 = 38, 38 ÷ 2 = 19. Figure 19. Figure 20 divides 40 by 2 and forgets the 2 end chairs. 40 is the number of chairs.

items.q: In the pattern 3n + 2, which term number has a term value of 47?
items.e: Solve 3n + 2 = 47. Undo + 2: 47 − 2 = 45. Undo × 3: 45 ÷ 3 = 15. Check: 3 × 15 + 2 = 47. 47 is the term value, not the term number. 143 finds term 47 instead.

items.q: The rule of a pattern is t = 5n − 7. Which term number has a value of 58?
items.e: Solve 5n − 7 = 58. Undo − 7: 58 + 7 = 65. Undo × 5: 65 ÷ 5 = 13. 10,2 subtracts 7 instead of adding. 283 finds term 58.

items.q: Is 75 a term value of the pattern 6n + 4?
c: No, the term number would not be a whole number
items.e: Solve 6n + 4 = 75: 75 − 4 = 71, and 71 ÷ 6 is not a whole number. Term 11 is 70 and term 12 is 76, so 75 is skipped. No.

items.q: The rule of a shrinking pattern is t = 90 − 6n. Which term number has a value of 24?
items.e: Solve 90 − 6n = 24. 90 − 24 = 66, so 6n = 66 and n = 11. Check: 90 − 66 = 24. 66 forgets to divide by 6. 19 adds 24 to 90 instead of subtracting.

items.q: Pattern A is 4n + 1 and pattern B is 2n + 11. For which term number do they have the same value?
items.e: Make a table. Term 4: 17 and 19. Term 5: 4 × 5 + 1 = 21 and 2 × 5 + 11 = 21. They match at term 5. 21 is the value, not the term number. 10 is 11 − 1.

items.q: A taxi charges R4,50 to start plus R2 for each kilometre. How much does an 8 km ride cost?
items.e: 2 × 8 = 16. Then R16,00 + R4,50 = R20,50. R16,00 forgets the R4,50 start. R52,00 adds first: (4,50 + 2) × 8. R36,00 charges R4,50 per kilometre.

items.q: The same taxi charges R4,50 to start plus R2 for each kilometre. A ride costs R30,50. How long was it?
items.e: Take off the start: R30,50 − R4,50 = R26. Each kilometre is R2: 26 ÷ 2 = 13 km. 15,25 km forgets the R4,50. 17,5 km adds the R4,50 instead of subtracting. 26 km forgets to divide by 2.

items.q: Elna has R45 and saves R15 each week. The skates cost R210. After how many weeks can she buy them?
items.e: Solve 15w + 45 = 210. She still needs R210 − R45 = R165. 165 ÷ 15 = 11 weeks. 14 weeks forgets the R45 she has. 17 weeks adds the R45 instead of subtracting.

items.q: A canoe rental in Algonquin Park has two plans. Plan A: R20 per hour. Plan B: R40 plus R12 per hour. For how many hours do both plans cost the same?
items.e: Make a table. Plan A: R20, R40, R60, R80, R100. Plan B: R52, R64, R76, R88, R100. At 5 hours both cost R100. 100 is the cost, not the hours. 8 is 20 − 12.

items.q: The tank starts with 150 ℓ of sap and collects 40 ℓ each day. It is full at 750 ℓ. After how many days is it full?
items.e: Solve 40d + 150 = 750. 750 − 150 = 600, and 600 ÷ 40 = 15 days. 18,75 days forgets the 150 ℓ already there. 22,5 days adds the 150 ℓ.
